brief.question: After RLHF fine-tuning made InstructGPT worse on standard public NLP benchmarks, what change to training did the authors use to win that accuracy back?

claims.text: During RLHF fine-tuning, the authors observed performance regressions compared to GPT-3 on certain public NLP datasets, notably SQuAD, DROP, HellaSwag, and WMT 2015 French to English translation.

The authors greatly reduced the performance regressions on these datasets by mixing PPO updates with updates that increase the log likelihood of the pretraining distribution (PPO-ptx), without compromising labeler preference scores.
Adding pretraining updates to PPO fine-tuning (PPO-ptx) mitigated the performance regressions on all datasets and even surpassed GPT-3 on HellaSwag.
Mixing in pretraining updates performed better than the simpler solution of increasing the KL coefficient.
Increasing the KL coefficient led to significant decreases in validation reward and never fully recovered on DROP and SQuAD.

brief.question: According to Kaplan et al., if model size is increased 8x, roughly how much must the dataset grow to avoid an overfitting penalty, and why?

claims.text: Kaplan et al. estimate that to avoid overfitting when training to within roughly 0.02 of convergence, the dataset size must satisfy D ≳ (5×10^3) N^0.74.
This relation shows that dataset size may grow sub-linearly in model size while avoiding overfitting.
The extent of overfitting depends predominantly on the ratio N^(α_N/α_D)/D.
The fitted exponents are α_N = 0.076 and α_D = 0.103.

brief.not_found: The excerpts do not give an explicit numeric answer for an 8x increase in model size; the required dataset growth can only be inferred from the stated power-law relation and fitted exponents, which the excerpts do not work out.

brief.question: According to LLM.int8(), at what model scale do the outlier features that break standard 8-bit quantization emerge, and how concentrated are they?

claims.text: Large magnitude outlier features emerge in all transformer layers starting at scales of 6.7B parameters.

When measured by number of parameters, the emergence of large magnitude features across all layers occurs suddenly between 6B and 6.7B parameters, with the percentage of layers affected increasing from 65% to 100%.
The number of sequence dimensions affected increases rapidly from 35% to 75% at this emergence.
The outlier features are highly systematic and represent at most 7 unique feature dimensions.
Up to 150k outliers can exist per 2048 token sequence for a 13B model.
The outlier features are incredibly sparse, making up only about 0.1% of all feature dimensions.
These outliers occur systematically for almost all sequence dimensions but are limited to specific feature/hidden dimensions.
